Google Inactive Account Manager vs Apple Legacy Contact (2026)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

Short answer: They solve the same problem for different ecosystems, and both are free, so use both if you have Google and Apple accounts. Google's Inactive Account Manager acts automatically after a period of inactivity and can share data with up to 10 people. Apple Legacy Contact needs an access key plus a death certificate.

Key facts

  • Verdict: Not either-or: set up both.
  • Google Inactive Account Manager: Free.
  • Apple Legacy Contact: Free (requires an Apple Account and a supported OS version).

Which should you choose?

Verdict: Not either-or: set up both. Google's is automatic and flexible but triggers on inactivity, not death. Apple's is triggered by verified death and gives broader account data, but excludes Keychain passwords and purchased media.

Google Inactive Account Manager

Free and essential if you use Google. Set it up today: after a period of inactivity you choose, Google notifies up to 10 people and can share selected data with them. Official site ↗

Apple Legacy Contact

Free and essential for iPhone users. Without it, even close family can find it very hard to get into iCloud photos and data. Official site ↗

Frequently asked questions

Google Inactive Account Manager vs Apple Legacy Contact: which is better?

They solve the same problem for different ecosystems, and both are free, so use both if you have Google and Apple accounts. Google's Inactive Account Manager acts automatically after a period of inactivity and can share data with up to 10 people. Apple Legacy Contact needs an access key plus a death certificate.

Should I use both?

Yes, if you use Google and Apple services. They cover different accounts and both are free.

Does Google need a death certificate?

Not for Inactive Account Manager. It triggers after the inactivity period you set. Without a plan, Google's deceased-user requests do require documentation.

Does either share passwords?

Neither shares your password. Apple excludes iCloud Keychain, and Google never provides login details.

What happens if I don't set them up?

Google can delete personal accounts inactive for 2 years, and Apple generally needs a court order or local equivalent.
